props.title: Dumb and Dumber
props.initialSlug: Two idiots' wild road trip to return a briefcase

sections.content: Dumb and Dumber (1994) marked a defining moment in slapstick comedy, launching the Farrelly Brothers' signature gross-out style and cementing Jim Carrey's incredible 1994 run alongside Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994) and The Mask (1994). The film's genius lies in its commitment to pure, unfiltered stupidity - Lloyd and Harry aren't just dim, they're gloriously, confidently moronic. This marked a departure from the more grounded comedic duos like Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987), embracing a new wave of boundary-pushing humor that influenced everything from There's Something About Mary (1998) to Anchorman (2004).

sections.content: The film's road trip structure became a template for countless buddy comedies that followed. While Road Trip (2000) and EuroTrip (2004) aimed for similar cross-country hijinks, none matched Dumb and Dumber's perfect chemistry between Carrey and Jeff Daniels. Daniels, known primarily as a dramatic actor, proved his comedy chops by matching Carrey's manic energy beat for beat. This unlikely pairing created a blueprint for future odd-couple comedies like Step Brothers (2008) and The Other Guys (2010).

The film's quotability factor remains unmatched, with lines like "So you're telling me there's a chance" entering permanent pop culture status. This level of memorable dialogue rivals only a handful of pure comedies like Caddyshack (1980) and Airplane! (1980). The Farrelly Brothers' direction balanced broad physical comedy with surprisingly sharp timing, creating set pieces that still hold up decades later. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Comedy

movies.slug: Ben Stiller's fashion satire follows similarly dim but lovable protagonists through increasingly absurd situations

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond just buddy comedies. Its mix of heart and crude humor created a template for the Judd Apatow-era comedies of the 2000s. Films like The 40-Year-Old Virgin (2005) and Knocked Up (2007) followed Dumb and Dumber's example of grounding outrageous comedy in genuine friendship. Even modern classics like The Hangover (2009) owe a debt to how Dumb and Dumber structured its escalating series of mishaps and misunderstandings.
